info.title: OpenDispatch
info.description: The REST half of the OpenDispatch API contract. SignalR board events and the offline-sync payloads are not describable here; they live in @opendispatch/contracts.

scheduledStart.description: When they are planned to arrive.

assignmentId.description: The identity of the stop it created or moved — the board has just drawn it.

sequence.description: Where it falls in the technician's run, counting from zero.

scheduledStart.description: When the technician is planned to start work.

travelMin.description: Minutes of driving to reach this stop from the previous one.

AssignmentExport.description: One stop, as it appears in `GET /export`.

id.description: The device's own id for the capture.

jobId.description: The job it was captured against.

serverId.description: The handle its bytes are stored under.

createdAt.description: When it was captured, by the device's clock.

AttachmentExport.description: One captured photo or signature's metadata, as it appears in `GET /export`.

AttachmentKind.description: What a technician captured, as the clients see it.

id.description: The capture's id — the one its device generated.

jobId.description: The job it was captured against.

contentType.description: What the bytes are, as the download will answer with.

contentUrl.description: Where to fetch the bytes, on this same API.

AttachmentResponse.description: One capture, without its bytes. An element of `GET /jobs/{id}/attachments`.

status.description: How far through its life it is — what colours the block.

requiredSkill.description: What a technician needs to take it.

estimatedDuration.description: How long the work should take — the width of the block.

latitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

address.description: Where it is, for a human.

BoardJobResponse.description: A job as the board shows it, over REST — the snapshot half of JobUpdated's delta.

name.description: Their name, as the lane is labelled.

skills.description:
What they are qualified for. Here for the same reason it is on the projection this mirrors: a
manual assignment may put work on somebody who does not hold the job's skill, and the board is
what shows the mismatch.

homeLat.description: Where the day starts and ends, in decimal degrees.

homeLng.description: Where the day starts and ends, in decimal degrees.

BoardRouteResponse.description: One technician's day, as it appears on the board over REST: a lane and a line on the map.

assignmentId.description: The stop's own identity — what a drag on the board reschedules.

sequence.description: Where it falls in the technician's run, counting from zero.

scheduledStart.description: When the technician is planned to start work.

travelMin.description: Minutes of driving to get here from the previous stop.

lateBy.description: How far past the promised window the work is planned to begin, or zero when it begins inside it.

BoardStopResponse.description: A planned visit, as it appears on a technician's lane over REST.

completedAt.description:
When the work actually finished. Only read when Status is
JobStatus.Completed; when it is omitted the server asks its own clock.

email.description: An email address, or `null` if there isn't one.

phone.description: A phone number, or `null` if there isn't one.

lines.description: What to charge for — time on the job, and parts fitted.

CreateInvoiceRequest.description: The body of `POST /jobs/{id}/invoice`. The job comes from the route.

locationId.description: Which of that customer's service locations it happens at.

requiredSkill.description: The skill a technician must have to take it.

estimatedDuration.description: How long the work should take once a technician is on site.

id.description: The identity of the job it created.

name.description: Their name, as it appears on the dispatch board.

skills.description: What they are qualified to work on. Empty is allowed — a trainee simply matches no skilled job.

latitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees between -180 and 180.

items.description: The customers on this page, by name.

total.description: How many the tenant has altogether.

page.description: Which page this is, counting from one.

pageSize.description: How many this page was allowed to hold.

CustomerPageResponse.description: One page of customers. The body of `GET /customers?page={n}&pageSize={n}`.

email.description: Their email address, or `null` if there isn't one.

phone.description: Their phone number, or `null` if there isn't one.

locations.description: The places they want work done, in the order they were added.

CustomerResponse.description: One customer, as the clients see them: who they are, how to reach them, and where they want work done.

id.description: Their identity, which is what a caller picks them by.

email.description: Their email address, or `null` if there isn't one.

phone.description: Their phone number, or `null` if there isn't one.

CustomerSummaryResponse.description: A customer as `GET /customers` lists them: enough to recognise and to reach, and nothing else.

dayStart.description: The instant the requested day opens, UTC.

dayEnd.description: The instant the requested day closes, UTC.

routes.description: One run per technician, each ordered by sequence. Technicians with nothing on are present and empty.

unassigned.description: Jobs promised inside the day that no technician has been given.

DispatchBoardResponse.description: The response from `GET /dispatch/board?day=`: a snapshot of the day.

customers.description: Every customer, with their service locations.

assignments.description: The plan: every stop, whichever technician it is on.

invoices.description: Every bill raised, with its lines and whether it is settled.

attachments.description: Every photo and signature captured, by metadata — not their bytes.

ExportResponse.description:
The whole of a tenant's business data — the response from `GET /export`, Document 1's
anti-lock-in feature: "your customers, your jobs, your data — on software you control."

status.description: Always `healthy`: a host that could not answer would not answer.

service.description: Which service replied, for a probe pointed at the wrong port.

jobId.description: The work that has just come in.

InsertJobRequest.description: The body of `POST /schedule/insert`: an emergency, named by the job it is for.

assignmentId.description: The stop that now exists for it.

scheduledStart.description: When the work is planned to start.

sequence.description: Where it falls in that technician's run, counting from zero.

displaced.description:
How many of that technician's other stops had to move along to make room. Zero when the job
went on the end of a day.

InsertJobResponse.description: The response from `POST /schedule/insert`: where the emergency went.

description.description: What it says on the invoice.

quantity.description: How many — hours for labour, units for parts. Fractions are ordinary.

unitPrice.description: The price of one, in whole currency units (dollars, not cents). Negative for a discount.

InvoiceLineRequest.description: One line to bill, as submitted to `POST /jobs/{id}/invoice`.

description.description: What it says on the invoice.

quantity.description: How many — hours for labour, units for parts.

unitPrice.description: The price of one, in dollars. Negative for a discount.

lineTotal.description: What this line adds to the invoice, in dollars.

InvoiceLineResponse.description: One billed line, as the clients see it.

lines.description: What it bills for, in the order the lines were added.

InvoiceResponse.description:
One invoice, as the clients see it — the response from `POST /jobs/{id}/invoice`, and the
shape every invoice takes in `GET /export`.

InvoiceStatus.description: Whether an invoice has been settled, as the clients see it.

items.description: The jobs on this page, soonest-promised first.

total.description: How many the tenant has altogether.

page.description: Which page this is, counting from one.

pageSize.description: How many this page was allowed to hold.

JobPageResponse.description: One page of jobs. The body of `GET /jobs?page={n}&pageSize={n}`.

JobPriority.description: How badly a job needs doing, as the clients see it.

locationId.description: Which of that customer's service locations it happens at.

latitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

requiredSkill.description: The skill a technician must have to take it.

estimatedDuration.description: How long the work should take once a technician is on site.

status.description: How far through its life the job is.

notes.description: What a technician wrote about it, or `null` if nobody has.

JobResponse.description: One job, as the clients see it: the demand, and nothing about the plan.

JobStatus.description: Where a job has got to in its life, as the clients see it.

LineItemKind.description: What a billed line is for, as the clients see it.

token.description: The bearer token — send it as `Authorization: Bearer {Token}`.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops being accepted.

travel.description: Cost of one minute of driving. The unit the other three are quoted in.

lateness.description: Cost of one minute past a job's promised window.

overtime.description: Cost of one minute worked past the end of a technician's shift.

unassigned.description: Cost of leaving a job undone, per unit of its priority.

ObjectiveWeightsRequest.description: What a good schedule is worth, as a caller states it. Optional on OptimizeScheduleRequest.

from.description: When the horizon to re-plan opens.

to.description: When it closes. Never earlier than From.

oneOf.description: What a good schedule is worth, or `null` for the engine's defaults.

planned.description: How many stops the day now has.

unassigned.description: The jobs no technician could take. Not a failure — see the remarks on `OptimizedDay`.

cost.description:
What the plan scores under the weights it was given. Only comparable against another response
for the same horizon under the same weights.

OptimizeScheduleResponse.description: The response from `POST /schedule/optimize`: what the optimiser did.

status.description: `healthy`, `degraded` or `unhealthy` — the worst status among the checks.

checks.description:
Each registered check by name, with its own status. An operator reading a 503 needs to know
which dependency is down; a single word makes them go and look.

label.description: What the customer calls it — "Home", "Unit 4", "the Croydon branch".

address.description: The postal address a technician would be given.

latitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees between -180 and 180.

id.description: The identity a job points at.

address.description: The postal address a technician would be given.

latitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Where it is, in decimal degrees.

ServiceLocationResponse.description: One of a customer's service locations, as the clients see it.

skills.description: The complete list they should have afterwards. Empty makes them a trainee again.

entity.description: What kind of thing this is — the same vocabulary an operation uses.

version.description: Its concurrency stamp as the server holds it.

oneOf.description:
The entity as the client should now hold it, or `null` when
Deleted is set — the two always agree.

deleted.description:
The entity is gone from this device's world: cancelled, or a stop re-optimised onto
somebody else's day. Removal has to be sayable, because a phone that is never told simply
keeps the stop and drives to it.

SyncChange.description: One entity as the server currently holds it, sent to a device that is behind.

opId.description: Which operation, by the id the device gave it.

reason.description: What kind of refusal it was, for the client to branch on.

message.description: Why, in terms fit to show the technician holding the phone.

SyncConflict.description: An operation the server would not apply, and why.

SyncConflictReason.description: The kinds of refusal a pushed operation can meet.

id.description:
The device's own identifier for this operation, and the idempotency key. A phone that
pushes, loses signal, and pushes again sends the same id, which is how the server knows
not to apply it twice.

entity.description: What kind of thing it happened to — `"job"`, `"line_item"`.

payload.description: The operation's own data, shaped by Type.

baseVersion.description:
The version of the entity the device was looking at when it acted. What a stale write is
judged against; the server's answer is authoritative either way.

clientTs.description:
When it happened on the device, which is not when it arrived. The ordering a technician
would recognise, and what last-write-wins on free text is decided by.

SyncOp.description:
One thing a technician did in the field: started a job, added a note, added a part,
finished. Queued on the device and pushed in batches (Document 2 §10).

changes.description: The entities that moved, as the server now holds them.

cursor.description:
The watermark to ask with next time. Opaque — the shape of the server's bookmark is not
part of the contract.

hasMore.description:
Whether the server stopped early and has more waiting. When `true`, pull again
with Cursor as soon as this page is applied; when `false`,
the device is up to date as of Cursor.

SyncPullResponse.description:
Everything that changed in a device's world since the cursor it asked with, and where it
now stands. The body of `GET /sync/pull?since={cursor}`.

SyncPushRequest.description:
A device emptying its queue: everything it did since it last got through, in the order it
did it. The body of `POST /sync/push`.

conflicts.description: The ops that were refused, each with a reason fit to show a technician.

cursor.description:
Where the device now stands in the change stream. Opaque — it is the server's watermark,
and a client that parses it is reading something it was not promised.

SyncPushResponse.description:
What the server made of a pushed batch. Authoritative: the device rebases onto this rather
than keeping its own opinion (Document 2 §10).

name.description: Their name, as it appears on the dispatch board.

skills.description: What they are qualified to work on, alphabetically.

latitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees.

TechnicianResponse.description: One technician, as the clients see them.

email.description: An email address, or `null` if there isn't one.

phone.description: A phone number, or `null` if there isn't one.

name.description: Their name, as it appears on the dispatch board.

latitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Their home base, in decimal degrees between -180 and 180.

UpdateTechnicianRequest.description:
The body of `PUT /technicians/{id}` — everything SetSkillsRequest and
SetShiftRequest do not own.

attachmentId.description: The id the device generated for the capture — the idempotency key.

jobId.description:
The job it was captured against. Carried here as the build text names it, but the route's own
`{id}` is what the endpoint actually acts on — the same convention every other
`/jobs/{id}/...` route in this API already follows, of not trusting a body to restate an id
the URL already carries. The two are checked against each other; a mismatch is refused rather
than silently resolved one way.

UploadAttachmentRequest.description:
The metadata half of `POST /jobs/{id}/attachments` — the multipart form's fields beside the
binary itself.

serverId.description:
The handle the server holds this content under. Opaque — a client stores it and does not parse
it, the same register as a sync cursor.

Bearer.description: The token POST /auth/login returns, sent as "Authorization: Bearer <token>".
